replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Pauline Nesbitt
replacements.fit: The composed closed eyes, loose tan waves, and steady stance favor a grounded period cowgirl name over a novelty choice.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Billie
replacements.fit: The happy expression, lively braids, and red field give Billie an upbeat rodeo rhythm that fits both portrait and surname.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Alice Greenough Orr
replacements.fit: The wide surprised face and vivid green eyes give Alice a curious, alert character read while the black hair keeps the full name crisp.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Joyce
replacements.fit: The beaming mouth and playful raised baseball prop make the bright, familiar Joyce feel warmer and more human than the previous place-like name.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Ardith
replacements.fit: The red background, turmeric hair, flat-up eyes, and grimace call for a tougher vintage name with real rodeo weight.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Vivian White
replacements.fit: Vivian matches the polished black hair, 3D glasses, and bright smile with a stylish Western-screen presence.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Elsa
replacements.fit: The snow-white hair, blue doll eyes, and ocean-blue field make Elsa an immediate visual fit while remaining an exact cowgirl-bank entry.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Florence Hughes Randolph
replacements.fit: The white brush prop, soft closed eyes, and fluffy gold hair support an artistic, old-fashioned name with calm authority.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Juanita Hackett Howell
replacements.fit: The dramatic scream, round eyes, black shower-like hair, and sky-blue field benefit from Juanita's strong classic Western cadence.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Kendra
replacements.fit: The basketball prop and alert stance make an athletic, contemporary cowgirl name fit better, while the tearful eyes keep it personable.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Fonda
replacements.fit: The blazing sun, drink prop, blue eyes, and wild braids create a broad cinematic-rodeo silhouette that the compact Fonda name carries well.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Mayisha
replacements.fit: The warm smile, deep complexion, gold curls, and cool blue background support a distinctive real honoree name with strong individuality.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Carole
replacements.fit: The proud expression, moon-candy hair, and baseball prop read as poised and classic, which Carole expresses without sounding costume-generated.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Deborah Copenhaver Fellows
replacements.fit: The blue eyes, black hair, heart sunrise, and serious mouth call for a strong, compassionate real-person name rather than another compound word.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Kristie
replacements.fit: The soccer ball, angry brows, and snow hair make this portrait read athletic and competitive, matching a real rodeo inductee name.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Janell
replacements.fit: The golden face, heart sunrise, coin, and tidy black hair give Janell a bright but grounded prize-winner quality.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Charmayne
replacements.fit: The fierce glare, scream, and hot-frizz hair need a championship-caliber name with energy and presence.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Margie Greenough Henson
replacements.fit: Round eyes, a broad beam, and copper frizz make Margie feel lively, friendly, and naturally collectible.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Jimmie
replacements.fit: The baseball, glare, and fluffy gold hair produce a sporty, determined portrait that suits this brisk rodeo name.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Lari
replacements.fit: The wine glass, crescent moon, loose tan waves, and relaxed smile favor a short mature Western name with an easy nighttime rhythm.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Rhonda
replacements.fit: The scarlet backdrop, laughing mouth, sour eyes, and dark hot-frizz hair give Rhonda the boldness this expressive portrait needs.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Pam
replacements.fit: The surprised eyes, black hair, baguette, and purple field already carry plenty of visual detail, so a clean short name balances the full name.

replacements.reference: ProRodeo Hall of Fame and WPRA inductee Jeana
replacements.fit: The basketball prop, raised gaze, and loose tan hair make Jeana feel active and human while pairing smoothly with the existing surname.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Jonnie Jonckowski
replacements.fit: The baseball, googly eyes, huge grin, braids, and white-cloud background give Jonnie a playful competitive charm.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Steely
replacements.fit: The grey stare, angry brows, fuzzy swirl, and red concentric background make Steely an unusually exact expression-and-color fit.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Eulalia Sister Bourne
replacements.fit: The blue doll eyes, dark complexion, loose waves, and overgrown landscape support a lyrical old-West name with real provenance.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Dessie Sawyer
replacements.fit: The bright smile, happy eyes, and brandy braids make Dessie feel warm, period-appropriate, and immediately character-like.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Gretchen Sammis
replacements.fit: Green stretched eyes, neutral mouth, and unruly orange frizz call for a firmer classic name that does not lean into the ice-cream prop.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Agnes
replacements.fit: The sour eyes, downturned mouth, dark loose hair, and blue field make the compact vintage Agnes a deliberate dry-humor fit.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Nancy Sheppard
replacements.fit: Snow hair, round eyes, and a broad smile make Nancy feel cheerful and familiar, balancing the busier pizza-derived surname.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Temple
replacements.fit: The moon-candy hair, messy-room setting, baseball, and cool expression give Temple an enigmatic but grounded collectible quality.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Hall of Fame honoree Fannie Sperry Steele
replacements.fit: The pink field, wild braids, green eyes, beer glass, and smile create a lively old-time cowgirl portrait that Fannie fits naturally.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Sabra
replacements.fit: The hot-frizz hair, grimace, sun, taco, and purple background make a compact hard-edged name more effective than another ornate form.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Kassie
replacements.fit: The baseball, beaming smile, brown eyes, and energetic frizz make Kassie a quick, athletic, friendly fit.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Veryl
replacements.fit: The crescent moon, tar-black hair, dark complexion, and happy eyes give Veryl a distinctive moonlit Western silhouette.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Buffy
replacements.fit: The swamp swirl, droopy eyes, snow hair, and oversized smile have a playful oddball energy that Buffy captures cleanly.

replacements.reference: 2026 WPRA competitor Cally
replacements.fit: The pink field, crescent moon, happy eyes, surprised smile, and brandy braids make Cally bright and spirited without overpowering the surname.

replacements.reference: National Cowgirl Museum Hall of Fame honoree Kay
replacements.fit: The white cloud, sky-blue background, green eyes, black hair, and beaming expression call for a light, direct name that keeps the full name airy.
